In Switzerland, 6,648 adults participated (response rate 30%), and the sample was drawn to be representative of about 5.6 million adults aged 16–65 residing in the country at the time of data collection. The notes state that analyses were conducted to ensure that non-response does not introduce significant bias, implying the use of survey design adjustments/weighting procedures, but the specific weight variable names are not provided in the excerpt. The report also excludes “doorstep” respondents when comparing across cycles, and it notes that some adults were not administered the doorstep questionnaire due to language barriers, which affects comparability of certain subgroup estimates.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note summarizes results from the Survey of Adult Skills 2023 for Switzerland, where adults aged 16–65 were assessed in three domains: literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving. The assessment was administered exclusively on digital tablets, and proficiency is reported on 500-point scales with proficiency levels derived from task success/failure and item difficulty. Switzerland’s mean performance is above the OECD average in all three domains (literacy 266, numeracy 276, adaptive problem solving 257). The note reports proficiency-level shares (e.g., literacy Level 1 or below: 22%; numeracy Level 1 or below: 19%; adaptive problem solving Level 1 or below: 25%) and highlights age gradients, with older adults (55–65) scoring lower than younger adults (25–34). It also documents associations between higher numeracy and labour force participation/wages, and between higher proficiency and well-being and civic engagement, while noting exclusions related to language barriers and doorstep administration for comparability.
